styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Hotpot, noodles and street snacks all day.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Old towns, river views and mountain-city life.

styles.label: Nightlife
styles.blurb: Neon skylines, river cruises and late-night eats.

stays.why: The central peninsula: walk to Hongya Cave, the riverfront and the main metro lines. Best for first-timers.
Across the river from the skyline; good views back at Jiefangbei and easy metro links. Slightly quieter nights.
South bank, near the Yangtze and the cableway area. Cheaper rooms and a local feel; a short metro ride to the centre.
University district with cheap eats and a busy station. Good value if you plan day trips by train.

food: Order Chongqing hotpot: a spicy bubbling broth with beef, tripe and vegetables. Ask for mild (微辣) if unsure; prices are often per dish, roughly ¥60–120 a person.
Try Chongqing xiaomian (small noodles) for breakfast or a cheap lunch, about ¥8–15 a bowl.
Snack streets and night markets are everywhere; Jiefangbei and the old town lanes are easy starting points. Pay by phone app or cash.
River fish and spicy chicken dishes are local favourites. Look for busy places with local diners.
Street stalls are cheap and tasty; drink bottled water and pick stalls with high turnover.
more_time: Add a Yangtze River Three Gorges day or overnight trip from the Chaotianmen docks; check schedules and prices on the day.
Visit Ciqikou old town for teahouses and snacks, or the Three Gorges Museum for regional history (check opening hours).
Take the Yangtze cableway across the river for views, then walk the south bank; queues can be long, so go early.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the old town, river views and a hotpot dinner; add a night for a Yangtze side trip.

month_notes: January: cold and damp, highs near 11°C. Pack warm layers; hotpot weather.
February: still cool, highs around 14°C. Fewer rain days than spring.
March: warming to 19°C but rain picks up (about 14 wet days). Bring an umbrella.
April: mild at 23°C, but one of the wettest months. Plan indoor backups.
May: warm and humid, highs 26°C, frequent rain. Light rain jacket helps.
June: hot and sticky, highs 29°C, many rainy days. Go out early and late.
July: hot, highs 32°C, humid. Carry water and take midday breaks.
August: the hottest month, highs 34°C. Limit midday walking; evenings are busy.
September: still warm at 28°C with plenty of rain. Watch for slippery stairs.
October: comfortable at 22°C, though rain is common. Good month for walking.
November: cooler at 17°C with fewer dry spells than autumn; layers advised.
December: cool and fairly dry, highs 12°C. Quiet season for sightseeing.

climate_guide.summary: Humid subtropical climate: mild winters, hot sticky summers, and rain in most months. Expect hills, stairs and haze.

items.title: Best months: October to December
items.text: Highs of 12–22°C and fewer rainy days. Comfortable for walking the hills and riverfront.

items.title: Hot, humid summer (June to August)
items.text: Highs of 29–34°C with high humidity. Move slowly, carry water and rest at midday.

items.title: Rain in most months
items.text: Spring and autumn are wettest, with 14–17 rain days. Pack a compact umbrella and grippy shoes.

items.title: Cool, damp winter
items.text: January highs near 11°C and lows around 6°C. Buildings can feel cold; bring warm layers.

items.title: Haze and mist
items.text: River mist and haze can hide the skyline. Views are clearest after rain or on cooler days.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Comfortable walking shoes for stairs and hills, a rain jacket, and light breathable clothes for summer.

transit.best: Metro for most trips; ride apps for hills, stairs and late nights.

modes.text: Fast, cheap and air-conditioned, with announcements in Mandarin and English. Lines 3 and 10 link the airport to the city.
Frequent and cheap, but signs are mostly in Chinese. Useful for short local hops.
Taxis are yellow and metered; few drivers speak English, so show your destination in Chinese. DiDi works well; set up the app before you arrive.
Not advised for visitors: steep, confusing roads and hard parking. Use metro and apps instead.
Expect stairs and hills everywhere. Biking is not advised in the centre. Wear good shoes.
A short Liangjiang ferry crosses the river for about ¥10. A cheap way to see the skyline from the water.
